content:
leila: Quick proposal: canonicalize sampling tokens at the edge so downstream fanout and dedupe use a stable key. Right now mobile SDKs and server producers each roll their own sample_id and we get mismatchy attribution + multiple reservoirs. Thoughts?

pav: Strong +1 for stable tokens. Biggest risk is trusting client-supplied ids. Clients can be buggy or malicious. Need a signing/validation step.

omar: We could have the gateway canonicalize token -> sample_token_signable and sign with edge HMAC. Downstream services validate signature before using it in reservoir counts. If invalid, treat as not-sampled.

sasha: Implementation tradeoff: sign every event costs CPU, and increases latency. Alternative: mint short-lived sample tokens (opaque id) at first gateway touch and return in response so subsequent events reuse it. But that needs client round-trip.

maria: Another option: use consistent hashing to map an incoming producer to a reservoir shard key (tenant + producer_id) without canonical token signing. Reservoirs are sharded by that hash so counts converge, but this doesn't solve duplicate event dedupe across producers.

leila: Good points. Requirements we want: 1) stable sampling decision across fanout (edge -> internal services), 2) verifiable provenance, 3) low latency overhead, 4) minimal memory churn for reservoir state.

pav: Proposal sketch: gateway computes sample_digest = HMAC(edge_key, concat(tenant, producer_id, event_root_id)) and emits header X-Redwood-Sample-Digest:sha256=... Downstream reservoir uses sample_digest mod N to pick shard. Also gateway includes X-Redwood-Sample-Source:edge-signed.

omar: For clients that already supply a sample_id, gateway should prefer client id but still emit signed_digest of the final canonical id so downstream can validate. That keeps backward compat while improving trust.

sasha: For de-dup we should use trace_root_id + sample_digest as canonical dedupe key and keep TTL 7 days in the de-dupe store. Rule: prefer message with highest envelope_version, then latest event_timestamp.

maria: Reservoir scaling: maintain per-tenant reservoir counters sharded by sample_digest%R where R is dynamic. If R changes (resharding), we risk count discontinuities. Need a resharding plan: do power-of-two increases and drain old shards gradually while emitting metrics to reconcile delta.

leila: Agreed. Also, for correctness we should accept signed sample_digest only when signature verifies against edge public key set; otherwise treat as unsigned and run sampling locally (fallback). Emit metric sample.signature.invalid.count.

pav: Operational metrics: sample.stable_ratio (percent events with canonical token), sample.fallback_rate, reservoir.overflow.count, dedupe.matches.count, sampling.latency.p95. Add alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% for 30m.

omar: Cost/perf tradeoff: signing in-path adds ~1-2ms p99 on our canary nodes. We can mitigate by offloading to a fast signing pool (translator workers) proxied at the gateway; keep fast passthrough for low-traffic tenants.

sasha: Security: rotate edge HMAC keys every 90 days. Use KMS to fetch keys and cache in signer processes. Include key-id in header: X-Redwood-Sample-Key-Id: k-2026-03.

maria: Backfill plan: for top-50 tenants, run a reconciliation job that replays raw events and re-derives canonical sample_digest so historical billing and SLOs align. For others, accept gradual correction as new events arrive.

leila: Acceptance tests: 1) fake client sends same trace with different client-generated sample_id -> gateway should canonicalize to same sample_digest. 2) invalid signature -> downstream must ignore signed header. 3) fanout to 3 services -> each uses the same reservoir decision.

pav: Quick header examples:

``
X-Redwood-Client-Sample-Id: sdk:abcd-1234
X-Redwood-Sample-Digest: sha256=977a...
X-Redwood-Sample-Key-Id: k-2026-03
X-Redwood-Sample-Source: edge-signed
``

leila: We need to update docs in obs/ingest for the header contract and add dashboard panels showing signed vs unsigned attribution. Also list of tenants enabled for canonicalization (feature-flagged).

sasha: Small callout: some downstream batch jobs ingest from S3 and won't receive headers. Those jobs should run the same derive function client-side (using public key verification) or mark data as legacy.

maria: I'll add playbook thresholds: fallback_rate > 0.5% for 1h, dedupe.matches spike (>5x baseline) -> pause translator, reservoir.overflow > threshold -> autoscale reservoir workers.

ingest-bot: deploy: sample-signer v1.0 -> prod-canary (10 tenants) :robot_face:

leila: Thanks. I'll open an RFC follow-up with the design + resharding plan + test vectors. Please drop any extra edge cases there.
